text: Correction, I misread your invite. You meant the RELAY's invite, as wsl-claude understood: the relay on spirit-3 mints one, and the face node installed beside it claims it to take its seat on that relay, as in the relay's first claim. Your key is installed separately, into puppet.json, as you said. So there's no puppet-pairing invite to build. wsl-claude's install script does both: mint and claim the relay seat, and write your key. Ignore my (a)/(b) question above.

UPDATED, and this replaces my earlier steps: you no longer bring an invite, and you don't update /root/SpiritOS (it follows your tags, and the scripts aren't in one). On spirit-3, as root: git clone https://github.com/andyflinn/SpiritOS.git /root/face/SpiritOS then /root/face/SpiritOS/bash/face-install <YOUR_NODE_KEY>. It installs your key as the face's owner, mints a one-day 'face' invite on the box's own relay and claims it, starts the face node, and prints the face node's key. If it asks for the Caddy block, that's bash/FACE.md step 3. Then on your node: accept the face node's key, and add face-domain.json and grants.json (FACE.md step 4). Test: curl -sS https://join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com/ should give 501 last-leg-not-built with your key. The root/systemd/Caddy parts run for the first time there; paste me anything red.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'write my invite directly into the relays data'.

Yes, and that's how wsl-claude is writing it: because you own spirit-3, the install mints the invite straight into the relay's own store with the relay's own code, then claims it from the face node and does all the connecting. There's nothing for you to bring or paste. I'll tell you when it's ready for you to run.

Yes, and that part is done: face-install writes the invite straight into the relay's data and claims it (ac05367), and installs your key as owner. What it CAN'T do from spirit-3 is the connecting on YOUR node, because your node isn't on that box. Three steps: accept the face node's key as a contact; write face-domain.json; add the 'join' grant. Go = I write one script for your side, run on your box after face-install: it takes the face node's key that face-install printed, and does all three through your node's own door (loopback), so you type one line on each machine. No = you do them by hand from FACE.md step 4.

No harm; we said the same thing. One check on your owner-side script: join's grant row must be { join: { to: <Andy's own node key> } }, so the owner answers 'owner of join is <his key>' and the face forwards to him. And if the grant goes in through the loopback door, make sure it's a door that already exists (fs.save into app/appFaceApp/ is writable), not a new verb, which would need his yes on the verb.

Andy's 'i ssh into spirit-3 ... clone ... /root/appFaceApp/ then run its bash commands?' is about your face-install (ac05367), so it's yours to answer. I'm not claiming it. One thing to tell him either way: the VPS already has the live relay's clone, /root/SpiritOS per your note; say whether the face node needs its own clone, since two clones means two Node processes and two update paths.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'clone into /root/appFaceApp/ then run its bash commands?' (my scripts).

Its own clone, not /root/SpiritOS. Exactly these two lines, as root:
git clone https://github.com/andyflinn/SpiritOS.git /root/face/SpiritOS
/root/face/SpiritOS/bash/face-install <YOUR_NODE_KEY>
Why not /root/SpiritOS: it follows your TAGS, and the face scripts aren't in a tag yet, so it doesn't have face-install; tagging would also restart the relay on all of master. Why a clone at all: the face node needs its own relay-state with its own key. Sharing the relay's folder would make the face and the relay the same party (one identity.json). So yes, two Node processes, as you approved, and two update paths: the relay moves on your tags, the face on master, by re-running its own face-install. Use /root/face/SpiritOS as written; the script expects that path, and a clone elsewhere would make it clone again.

Your side's script is ready (d011d41). One line on each machine now:
ON spirit-3 (root): git clone https://github.com/andyflinn/SpiritOS.git /root/face/SpiritOS then /root/face/SpiritOS/bash/face-install <YOUR_NODE_KEY>. It prints the face node's key at the end.
ON YOUR BOX, in your SpiritOS checkout after a git pull: node bash/face-owner.js <FACE_NODE_KEY>. It lets the face node in, writes face-domain.json, and grants 'join' to your node, merged with any grants you already have; it refuses to change a 'join' held by someone else.
Then: curl -sS https://join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com/ should give 501 last-leg-not-built naming your key.
Found and fixed on the way: your node (and the face node) could only accept a contact it had already seen, so both scripts now look the key up first. Without that the face would have ignored your answers. Tested against a throwaway node; spirit-3 is still the first real run of the root/Caddy parts.
